AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: The authors describe a minimally invasive surgical technique to re-establish corneal sensibility in a patient with neurotrophic keratopathy with the supraorbital nerve harvested endoscopically.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Pedicled contralateral supraorbital nerve was harvested endoscopically through small eyelid crease and scalp incisions and transferred to the affected eye.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Endoscopic corneal neurotization was successfully performed with restoration of corneal sensibility and corneal epithelial integrity.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The use of an endoscope allows for a minimally invasive approach to successful corneal neurotization with the supraorbital nerve.
